clue.text: As hands go to strike, sensible to get behind!

indicators.note: the word for sensible is told to come after, so it follows the word for strike

parts.note: to clock someone is slang for to hit or strike them
wise means sensible

explanation.surface: Someone urges a sensible person to back a strike, with a cry of encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' looks like workers, which suits 'strike', but it means a clock's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock hands move in this direction, so it describes the way they travel round the dial.

clue.text: I'm surprised US broadcaster limits alcohol

indicators.note: to limit is to bound on both sides, so the network's letters enclose the drink

parts.note: CBS is a major American television network
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A shocked viewer learns an American network restricts drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbs is a mild British exclamation of surprise, an interjection like 'goodness me'.

clue.text: Actor coached with one in test of speech

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for test

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

indicators.note: with the numeral included, so it is placed inside the jumbled actor
coaching puts an actor through drills, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A thespian is trained for an elocution examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coached' rearranges ACTOR into ATORC; 'with' one in it gives ATORIC, which goes 'in' ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratorical is the adjective relating to oratory, the art of public speaking.

clue.text: Finally struck margin on European food

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the next word

parts.note: an edge is a margin or border
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: At last a deal is struck on the fringe of European food policy.
explanation.walkthrough: KEDGEREE is a British-Indian dish of rice, flaked smoked fish and eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is a cooked dish, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Victor's wife leaving ring circling bull

indicators.note: the wife departs, so her letter is taken away from the word for victor

parts.note: a victor is a winner
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies

explanation.surface: A champion's spouse walks out of the arena where a bullfight is held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' and 'bull' suggest a bullring, but on a dartboard or target the inner is the ring round the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target, the inner is the band immediately surrounding the central bullseye.

clue.text: Smart little Euphemia collects just over 100 books

indicators.note: the pet name gathers the numeral into itself

parts.note: Effie is a pet form of the name Euphemia
CI is 101 in Roman numerals, just above a hundred
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A clever girl gathers a library of slightly more than a hundred volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart in the sense of competent and well-run is close to efficient.

clue.text: Left revolutionary in charge of hot line?

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the word for left is read backwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A left-wing rebel runs an emergency telephone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot line' suggests a crisis phone link; the question mark admits it is a line of latitude in a hot region.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are latitude lines bounding the warmest zone of the Earth.

clue.text: Nice way to host knight, ancient character

indicators.note: the street receives the knight as a guest, enclosing it

parts.note: rue is French for street, and Nice is a French city
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A pleasant road plays host to a knight of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective pleasant, but it is the French city, hence a French word for way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rune is a letter of the old Germanic alphabets, an ancient written symbol.

clue.text: Small articles breach crazy paper's title

indicators.note: these letters break into the word for crazy, splitting it

parts.note: mad means crazy
the and a are the definite and indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Little news stories break through a wacky newspaper's headline.
explanation.definitionFit: A masthead is the name of a newspaper printed in large type at the top of the front page.

clue.text: Plan for a stack in Perth to be withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawing pulls back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: lum is Scots for a chimney stack, and Perth is in Scotland

explanation.surface: A proposal for a chimney in Perth is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perth' might suggest Australia; here it marks a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula is a set method or recipe for doing something, effectively a plan.

clue.text: Rug and anorak more than enough to cover African

indicators.note: the words rug and anorak hold the answer within them, with letters to spare at each end

explanation.surface: A blanket plus a waterproof jacket is ample clothing for someone from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ugandan is a native of Uganda, a country in East Africa.

clue.text: Gather fuel blanketing heart of Ireland

indicators.note: the fuel wraps around the central letter like a blanket

parts.note: peat is dug and burned as fuel

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so the middle letter of the word Ireland

explanation.surface: Collect turf to cover the Irish heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: Peat is famously cut for fires in Ireland, which makes the surface coherent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold made by gathering cloth, so pleat and gather are synonyms in sewing.

clue.text: Going by live data, microbe mutates with it

indicators.note: a mutation changes form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lab report on how a bug evolves, based on current readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Biometric systems identify people from measurements of their living bodies, such as fingerprints.

clue.text: Count 150 bare pens on island

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it
to pen is to enclose, so the naked word holds the numeral

parts.note: nude means bare
CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A nobleman keeps a hundred and fifty naked animals in pens on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To count someone in a total is to include them.

clue.text: Blue Berets' former muscle man not bargained for

parts.note: UN peacekeepers wear blue berets
ex means former
pec is short for a pectoral muscle
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: An ex-peacekeeper turned bodybuilder was more than anyone had reckoned on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not bargained for is a surprise, which is what unexpected describes.

clue.text: Heroine Jane securing current high-rise retreat

indicators.note: the surname holds the symbol fast inside it

parts.note: Jane Eyre is the heroine of Charlotte Brontë's novel
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A literary heroine gets hold of a fashionable tower-block hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest on a crag, and by extension any lofty secluded dwelling.

clue.text: Complete journey on bullet train?

parts.note: a journey there and back is so named, and a bullet is also a round, so the trip of a round puns on the high-speed train

explanation.surface: A traveller books an outward and return ticket on Japan's high-speed railway.
explanation.walkthrough: A bullet is called a round, so its trip is the punning second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey to a place and back again is a full circuit, the usual name for a return ticket's trip.

clue.text: Concealed stock ready for auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is as heard rather than spelt

parts.note: ready, or readies, is slang for cash

explanation.surface: Hidden reserves of money are waiting for the accountant checking the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' suggests an accountant, but means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store of goods or weapons.

clue.text: Daily column includes a drawing

parts.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day

indicators.note: the abbreviation takes the letter inside it

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature carries an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper, which 'column' supports, but it is a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A charcoal is a sketch made with sticks of charred wood.

clue.text: Worry about troops governed by D-notice

indicators.note: the troops sit between the two parts of the D-notice, under its control

parts.note: D plus notice, an ad being a notice
RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of army troops

explanation.surface: Concerns about soldiers silenced by a British government press-gagging order.
explanation.walkthrough: A D-notice is a British official request to the press not to publish something on security grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to fear it greatly, to worry about it in advance.

clue.text: Child departs, giggling, scratching head

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: giggling is laughter

explanation.surface: A youngster leaves, sniggering and scratching their head.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a female child of her parents.

clue.text: Immoderate posh officer joins gunners

parts.note: U means upper-class
Lt is short for lieutenant
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: An upper-crust officer signs up with the artillery and goes too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as an adjective means extreme, going beyond moderate bounds.

clue.text: Trouble with English sailors netting duck's wing part

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: the sailors catch the round letter in their net

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
a duck is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: English sailors cause trouble trying to catch a duck by the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is the hinged flap on an aircraft's wing used to control roll.

clue.text: Insert another cartridge left over in study

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the word for study

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A shooter puts in another round left over from practice.
explanation.definitionFit: To reload a gun is to load it again with fresh ammunition.

clue.text: Fish with twit on banks

indicators.note: the two letters form banks on either side of the fool

parts.note: re means on or concerning
an ass is a twit

explanation.surface: An angler goes fishing with an idiot on the riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish of rocky coasts.

clue.text: River Ure guide undergoes training, as is proper

indicators.note: training reshapes, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire river guide gets coaching, as is only right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergoes training' rearranges URE and GUIDE into DERIGUEU; R for River ends the answer. The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: De rigueur is French for required by etiquette, meaning strictly correct or obligatory.

clue.text: One who regrets maybe taking in Liberal leader

indicators.note: the regretter takes the letter inside

parts.note: to rue is to regret, so a ruer is one who regrets

explanation.surface: A remorseful party member welcomes the Liberal chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler governs a country, so is its leader.

clue.text: Carp, the sixth to be found in shrunken state

indicators.note: the numeral is located inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation of California, the state cut short
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A fish, the sixth one caught, is discovered in a withered condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the fish but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavil is to raise trivial objections, which is what carping means.

clue.text: Star, say, visiting Virginia

indicators.note: the example pays a visit, going inside the state

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: A celebrity, for instance, is touring Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: Kid in stories not exactly well-behaved, for example

indicators.note: the child goes inside the fibs

parts.note: stories are lies, as in telling stories
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A child telling fibs is hardly a model of good behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not exactly well-behaved' is itself understatement by negation, an instance of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech that affirms by denying the opposite, as in 'not bad' for good.

clue.text: Asian, one chasing a lover around Grand Hotel

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the numeral comes last
the lover goes round the two letters

parts.note: a fan is a devotee or lover
G is slang for a grand, a thousand
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man pursues his sweetheart around a luxurious hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afghani is a native of Afghanistan, a country in Asia.

clue.text: Separate trip taking in golf game

parts.note: to part is to separate

indicators.note: the trip encloses the letter

parts.note: a ride is a short trip
G is Golf in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Split a journey to fit in a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' means wild animals shot for sport, not a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a game bird, hunted and eaten.
